canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1980-1982
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The final volume in the Selected Letters series, covering the last years of Dick's life, opens with an extraordinary passage in which Dick describes what he calls his 'second theophany' -- which he considered the most treasured moment of his life -- standing in his kitchen with his friend Ray Torrence (referenced in Dick's story 'I Hope I Shall Arrive Soon,' also known as 'Frozen Journey') at about eleven in the morning, as Torrence was about to return to Northern California after staying overnight.
page_summary:
The final volume in the Selected Letters series, covering the last years of Dick's life, opens with an extraordinary passage in which Dick describes what he calls his 'second theophany' -- which he considered the most treasured moment of his life -- standing in his kitchen with his friend Ray Torrence (referenced in Dick's story 'I Hope I Shall Arrive Soon,' also known as 'Frozen Journey') at about eleven in the morning, as Torrence was about to return to Northern California after staying overnight. Dick notes the experience was self-authenticating and something he discussed with even his closest friends only rarely. The volume documents his final creative period, spanning the completion of The Transmigration of Timothy Archer and his continuing work on the Exegesis.

**Why it matters.** As the final documentary record of Dick's correspondence before his death in March 1982, this volume is irreplaceable for understanding his state of mind at the height of his philosophical ambition and at the close of his life, including a previously under-examined 'second theophany' distinct from the more famous 2-3-74 events.

*The letters' proximity to Dick's death gives this volume a documentary finality the earlier volumes in the series do not carry.*
